title: Depth write in shader depends on discard instruction presence
body: ### Tested versions - Reproducible in 4.5.0 Net stable with Forward renderer ### System information Godot v4.5.stable.mono - Windows 10 (build 19045) - Multi-window, 2 monitors - Vulkan (Forward+) - dedicated NVIDIA GeForce RTX 3060 (NVIDIA; 32.0.15.6094) - Intel(R) Core(TM) i9-10900F CPU @ 2.80GHz (20 threads) - 63.91 GiB memory ### Issue description While writing custom depth value in spatial shader I noticed that the object with assigned shader displays as completely transparent (and working as a "mask" for other objects), together with that its deth value is calculated differently from others. Adding `discard` instruction completely fixes that behavior even if instruction itself is never called (and probably is even cut by shader compiler). Commenting line with `discard` instruction restores that weird behavior. Shader with instruction: Shader without instruction: ### Steps to reproduce Simplest shader to reproduce that behaviour: ```glsl shader_type spatial; render_mode unshaded; void fragment() { // fixes weird shader behaviour even if instruction is not called if (false) discard; ALBEDO = vec3(1.0, 0.0, 0.0); DEPTH = 0.5; } ``` Commenting line with `discard` instruction will result with weird behaviour ### Minimal reproduction project (MRP) Here is a small project with a single red quad with shader and background torus: [DepthBugReproduce.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/24038956/DepthBugReproduce.zip) Commenting line with `discard` instruction will result with weird behaviour:
